title: Balboa crosses the Isthmus of Panama
summary: On 1 September 1513 Vasco Nunez de Balboa sailed to Acla at the narrowest part of the Panama isthmus and set out across it with nearly 200 Spaniards and many native carriers. He first sighted the sea he called the South Sea from a hill on 25 or 27 September, and on the 29th his party reached the surf at the Gulf of San Miguel. He claimed the sea and its shores for the Spanish Crown.

uncertainty.note: Sighting date is 25 or 27 September (World History Encyclopedia) or 27 September (Encyclopedia.com, which also gives 13 September elsewhere).

reviewer_note: World History Encyclopedia says 200 conquistadors and over 1,000 native bearers; Encyclopedia.com says nearly 200 Spaniards and hundreds of Indian carriers; the summary keeps nearly 200 and many. Linda Hall says no one knows where the sighting happened, so only two waypoints are used (fewer than the 3 asked). Encyclopedia.com has an inconsistency (13 September in one passage, 27 September in another). Indigenous allies and guides are not named on any page opened. Acla position: Wikidata. The return to Darien in January 1514 (Encyclopedia.com) has no named place, so no third stop.

beats.caption: On 1 September 1513 Balboa sails to Acla, at the narrowest part of the isthmus, and starts across with nearly 200 Spaniards and carriers.
After sighting the ocean from a hill around 25 to 27 September, the party reaches its waves on the 29th at the Gulf of San Miguel.
Balboa claims the new sea, called the Southern Sea, and all lands bordering it for the Spanish Crown.
